criterion_A_rank_flip.rationale: An interaction contrast, not two separate comparisons. A flip means the RANKING reverses; D>0 is exactly that statement and is invariant to any oracle-level shift that affects all settings equally. The bootstrap is hierarchical because the claim is about landscape CLUSTERS: resampling seeds alone treats the 2 oracles per cluster as the entire population and understates uncertainty about generalising to other oracles of the same type. With only 2 oracles per cluster this test has low power BY CONSTRUCTION -- that is the honest cost of a cheap Phase 0, and it biases toward PIVOT rather than toward a false GO.
criterion_A_rank_flip.statement: There exist at least two landscape clusters whose winning exploration setting differs, and the difference is larger than seed variance.
criterion_A_rank_flip.test: For each backbone and each ordered pair of clusters (c1, c2) with argmax_e AUC(c1,e) = e1 != e2 = argmax_e AUC(c2,e): form the interaction contrast D = [AUC(c1,e1) - AUC(c1,e2)] + [AUC(c2,e2) - AUC(c2,e1)]. HIERARCHICAL bootstrap (10,000 resamples): resample oracles within each cluster WITH replacement, then seeds within each resampled oracle. The pair counts as a confirmed flip iff the 95% percentile CI of D excludes 0. A seed-only bootstrap is also reported as an optimistic bound, but the hierarchical interval is the one that gates the decision.
criterion_A_rank_flip.threshold: at least 2 confirmed flipped cluster pairs, within a single backbone

criterion_B_diagnostic.rationale: alpha=0.10 and not 0.05: Phase 0 is a SCREEN with n=8 oracles, and is explicitly underpowered. Criterion B asks 'is there a signal worth chasing', not 'is there a publishable effect'. Phase 1 (23 oracles) is the confirmatory test and will use alpha=0.05. Declaring this split here is what keeps Phase 1 confirmatory rather than a second bite at the same apple.
criterion_B_diagnostic.statement: At least one cheap landscape diagnostic correlates with the winning exploration setting across oracles.
criterion_B_diagnostic.test: Spearman rho between each diagnostic feature and the winning-setting index (0=low, 1=mid, 2=high) across the 8 oracles, for the LM backbone. Exact permutation p-value (all 8! = 40,320 permutations enumerated). Holm-Bonferroni correction across the diagnostic features tested.

metric_definition: PMO AUC-top-10: trapezoidal integral of mean top-10 reward against the number of unique canonical SMILES evaluated, normalised by max_oracle_calls. Reimplemented to match mol_opt/main/optimizer.py::top_auc exactly.
prohibited: Adding or dropping oracles after seeing results.
Changing the exploration-setting ladder after seeing results.
Adding diagnostic features after seeing results (the feature list is frozen in Part 8 and hashed with this document).
Reporting a cluster pair as a flip without the bootstrap CI.
Running more seeds and reporting only the favourable subset. If more seeds are run, ALL are reported.
title: Landscape-Conditional Exploration — Phase 0 falsification

verdict_consequences.GO: Proceed to Phase 1 (full 23-oracle characterisation) as written.
verdict_consequences.PARTIAL: The landscape dependence is real but our diagnostics do not capture it. Proceed to Phase 1 for C1 (characterisation) only; redesign the diagnostic feature set before attempting the controller. Downgrade venue expectation to a benchmark/characterisation contribution.
verdict_consequences.PIVOT: The premise is dead: exploration settings do not flip with landscape. Do NOT proceed to Phase 1. Switch to the proxy-gap sibling direction. Write up the null result as a short note -- it is informative, because the field has assumed this dependence since PMO without testing it directly.

verdict_rule.GO: criterion A passes AND criterion B passes
verdict_rule.PARTIAL: criterion A passes AND criterion B fails
